reviews.title: Disappointed – Paid for features that disappear after onboarding
reviews.text: Review: I bought an annual membership specifically for the real-time camera form correction and posture tracking featured in their ads. Unfortunately, the live stick-figure overlay is only active during the baseline assessment. Once you start regular workouts, it functions like any basic workout app without live camera feedback. Total bait-and-switch. Save your money if you are looking for real-time form guidance during actual exercise sets.

reviews.title: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Absolutely changed the way I train
reviews.text:
I started strength training about a year ago along with my GLP-1 journey. As a lifelong cardio person, I had no idea what I was doing, felt self conscious in the weights section, so I first used an expensive virtual coaching program and in person hours at the gym to build the habit.

Once I had the basics, I wanted something more flexible and sustainable — and Zing has been IT.

It gives me personalized workouts, lets me choose my equipment, workout length, and location, swap exercises, follow clear demos, pause when needed, track progress, and even connect Spotify. Probably does way more than I use for.

Honestly, for anyone who NO longer needs human oversight and reinforcement, Zing gives you EVERYTHING you need to keep going. Flexible, smart, easy to use, and worth every penny.

reviews.title: Good idea, poorly applied
reviews.text: I would like to say this is a great app for people who are trying to get back into health that have no training in fitness.  The AI is the best feature who is there all the time with quality information.  However, the workouts are generic, have no variance, or customization unless you manually do it yourself.  If you read their Science behind the app and methodology, just expect the exact opposite when it comes to workouts.  Rinse and repeat 3 sets of 8-12 reps.  With all the data they have more than any personal trainer could dream of, they do nothing with it to help their customers.  Weight adaptation is never accurate.  Great idea, poorly executed.

reviews.title: Unfair refund policies
reviews.text:
I’m disappointed with Zing Coach’s refund policy. I never even had the chance to use the app due to a medical condition, yet when my membership renewed, I was still charged.

To make matters worse, the renewal email was sent to my promotions folder, which I don’t regularly check. By the time I saw it and reached out to request a cancellation and refund, I was told I was outside their 48-hour window. I was charged on April 28, 2026, and contacted them on May 1, 2026—just a few days later. That’s hardly an unreasonable timeframe, especially considering I never used the service.

It’s frustrating to see companies enforce such rigid policies without considering real-life circumstances. If a service hasn’t been used, especially within days of being charged, there should be some flexibility.

Overall, this felt like a waste of money, and the lack of understanding or accommodation has left a very negative impression.
